prove.sourceFindings:
Minor documentation imprecision, with no safety impact under the model's ReinitFrames.

The claim: UPG `upgrades/registry/libraries/ProxyUpgradeRowLib.sol:119-120` says "The verification is a separate pass after every swap, so a reinitializer that moves any proxy of the row set is caught too."

Where it holds: only for row sets with one row per proxy. In general it holds for the last row naming each proxy. Proved, assuming each reinitializer moves at most its own proxy: ReinitMovesAreCaughtOnDistinctRows and ReinitMovesAreCaughtOnLastRow.

Why duplicate rows can reach it:
- `applyTransition` (`:102-113`) does not re-validate rows. It checks only `requireCode` (`:107`) and `domain()` (`:108-111`).
- `CTMUpgradeExecutor.applyInfrastructureUpgrade` (`executors/CTMUpgradeExecutor.sol:64-67`) and `CoreUpgradeExecutor.applyL1Upgrade` (`executors/CoreUpgradeExecutor.sol:33-36`) accept any `IProxyUpgradeTransition` from the owner.
- `validateRows` runs only in a genuine `ProxyUpgradeTransition`'s constructor (`objects/ProxyUpgradeTransition.sol:36`).

How it fails (DuplicateRowHidesReinitMove): a non-genuine object can carry two rows on one proxy. A reinitializer can move its own proxy to the later row's `expectedOldImpl`, and the later row then moves it back to the target. The call succeeds and the move is not caught. Concretely, row 6:10->12, whose reinitializer moves 6 to 11, reverts alone but succeeds when followed by 6:11->12.

Impact: the net effect is still the first row's source-checked edge (OnlyNamedEdgesAcrossCallAnyRows), so replay safety holds for any object. Only the sentence overstates what the pass catches.

A second, weaker case needs authority a reinitializer normally lacks: even for valid rows, a reinitializer that moves another row's proxy to that row's source before the row runs is not caught (ReinitLeakMovesNamedProxyOffEdge).

Context, not a bug: the parameter is documented as "The write-once transition approved by governance" (`executors/ICTMUpgradeExecutor.sol:35`, `executors/ICoreUpgradeExecutor.sol:17`). Only off-chain review checks the object's code identity and its rows (`protocol-docs/ecosystem-upgrade.md:354`).

review.sourceFindingAssessment:
The finding is real but minor: it is documentation only. ProxyUpgradeRowLib.sol:119-120 claims that "a reinitializer that moves any proxy of the row set is caught too". That holds only when each proxy has one row, or more generally for the last row naming each proxy.

Why non-genuine objects can reach applyRows:
- applyTransition (ProxyUpgradeRowLib.sol:102-113) checks only requireCode (:107) and domain() (:108-111), then runs applyRows on rows() (:112).
- applyRows (:121-148) never calls validateRows.
- Only ProxyUpgradeTransition's constructor runs validateRows (objects/ProxyUpgradeTransition.sol:36).
- CTMUpgradeExecutor.sol:64-67 and CoreUpgradeExecutor.sol:33-36 accept any IProxyUpgradeTransition from the owner.

The counterexample: a non-genuine object with rows [6:10->12 with init, 6:11->12]. If the reinitializer of 12 rewrites its own proxy's EIP-1967 slot to 11 (possible, since it runs by delegatecall in the proxy's storage), the second row's check at :131 passes and the swap at :138 runs without init. The second loop (:142-147) then sees 12 for both rows, so the call succeeds and the move goes uncaught. I checked this in the Lean model (DuplicateRowHidesReinitMove) and by hand against the Solidity.

Impact: the net effect is still the first row's source-checked edge (OnlyNamedEdgesAcrossCallAnyRows), so replay safety holds. Governance approval and off-chain review (protocol-docs/ecosystem-upgrade.md:354) are the only checks on duplicate rows.

The second case, ReinitLeakMovesNamedProxyOffEdge, is a valid countermodel, but it needs a reinitializer with authority over another proxy. The prover correctly calls it weaker.

The other applyRows caller is RegistryBootstrapMigration.sol:276. The prover does not mention it, and it is outside the claim. It applies toRows of its own manifest after validate(), so it adds no new exposure.

prove.sourceFindings:
Main finding (a robustness gap; it needs governance to approve a non-genuine object). ChainTypeManager.replaceUpgradeTransition (ChainTypeManager.sol:429-448) never checks that the replacement's oldProtocolVersion() equals the slot it writes. It writes slot `_expectedTransition.oldProtocolVersion()` (:433, :447). _requireSameDeparture compares only fromRelease() (:477-483).

Two readers locate a committed transition by its self-reported oldProtocolVersion():
- CTMUpgradeExecutor.upgradeChain (CTMUpgradeExecutor.sol:91-97);
- replaceUpgradeTransition itself (:433-437).

So once a replacement that misreports its slot is installed (a non-CTMTransition object; a genuine one derives the version from fromRelease, CTMTransition.sol:61-64):

(i) Every upgradeChain(t, id) for a chain at that version reverts TransitionNotCommitted, whatever t is, and this lasts (NonGenuineReplacementBricksUpgradeChain, MisreportingSlotStaysFrozen). This includes the replacement itself, which is what the NatSpec says to pass: "after a replacement, the replacement" (ICTMUpgradeExecutor.sol:55-56). It also contradicts the authority matrix, which lists upgradeChain as the executors' path for upgradeChainFromVersion (docs/registry-driven-upgrades.md:401).

(ii) The slot can never be replaced again (MisreportingSlotIsFrozen): replacing the bad object looks it up at the version it reports, and any other `expected` fails the compare. This contradicts "A transition already committed for a departed version can be repaired without moving the CTM" (protocol-docs/ecosystem-upgrade-coordination.md:171) for that slot. Only commit and replace write upgradeTransition (_recordTransition, :469), so the only fix left is a CTM implementation swap.

Chains can still cross the edge through the chain admin's direct Admin.upgradeChainFromVersion or the owner's forward of CTM.upgradeChainFromVersion. Safety and the routing headline are unaffected.

Precondition: governance approves the non-genuine object. The CTM trusts governance for this ("its construction is verified off-chain", ChainTypeManager.sol:405-407).

Suggested one-line fix in replaceUpgradeTransition: `if (_replacement.oldProtocolVersion() != oldProtocolVersion) revert ...`.

Doc imprecision: protocol-docs/ecosystem-upgrade-coordination.md:178 says a replacement "departs from the SAME release object (and so the same version)". The parenthetical holds only for genuine CTMTransition objects. The CTM indexes slots by the object's own report, which nothing compares with the release's version.

review.sourceFindingAssessment:
The finding is real. The CTM never checks that a replacement reports the slot it is written to. Every claim below was checked independently against upgrade-e561b9cc2:
- replaceUpgradeTransition (l1-contracts/contracts/state-transition/ChainTypeManager.sol:429-448) writes the slot `_expectedTransition.oldProtocolVersion()` (:433, :447 → _recordTransition :469). Nothing compares `_replacement.oldProtocolVersion()` with that slot. _requireSameDeparture (:477-483) compares only fromRelease(). _requireSameDeadline (:488) and _requireExecutable (:441) do not check the version either.
- CTMUpgradeExecutor.upgradeChain (upgrades/registry/executors/CTMUpgradeExecutor.sol:91-97) looks up `upgradeTransition(_transition.oldProtocolVersion())` and requires it to equal `_transition`. ChainTypeManager.upgradeChainFromVersion (:623-626) passes that version on, and Admin.upgradeChainFromVersion (Admin.sol:539-541) requires `s.protocolVersion == _oldProtocolVersion`.
- (i) Once slot v holds an object that reports w ≠ v, upgradeChain(t, id) reverts for every t when the chain is at v. For t with t.old = v, the slot holds the bad object, not t. For the bad object itself, slot w does not hold it. For any other w, Admin rejects the version.
- (ii) Only _recordTransition writes upgradeTransition, and only commit (:421) and replace (:447) call it; grep confirms. A commit writes slot protocolVersion, which is above v. A replace that rewrites slot v needs an `expected` that reports v and is committed at v, and no such object exists. So the slot is frozen short of a CTM implementation swap.
- The chain-side path does not read oldProtocolVersion(): the only callers in non-test code are CTMUpgradeExecutor.sol:80/91/105 and ChainTypeManager.sol:415/433. So the chain admin's direct call (ZKChainBase.sol:126-131 admits the admin, and Admin.sol:546 exempts it from the ServerNotifier gate) and a forwarded CTM call still cross the edge.
- A genuine CTMTransition derives old from fromRelease.protocolVersion() (CTMTransition.sol:61-64, 172-174), so the bug needs governance to approve a non-genuine object. The cited NatSpec (ICTMUpgradeExecutor.sol:56), authority matrix (docs/registry-driven-upgrades.md:401) and coordination doc (:171, :178) say what the prover quotes.
- Severity is low (a robustness or defense-in-depth gap under a trusted-governance assumption), and the one-line fix suggested is correct. Two small corrections: the replacement must also pass _requireExecutable and _requireSameDeadline (:441, :443), which an arbitrary contract can; and there are three getter-lookup readers, not two.

headlines.meaning: Take any config K, states s s', and a successful transaction FRun K s cs s'. Here cs lists a forward's calls plus the calls its targets make in turn, each with its own msg.sender. Premise (c.Covered K): every call's sender is neither the migration K.M nor 0, and every call is in the label set (not a renounceOwnership and not a CTM code swap). Conclusions: (1) ARun K s (cs.flatMap Call.labels) s' holds, i.e. the forward is a run of Authority's existing labels; (2) every one of those labels is an other-actor label (nominate/accept/transferPA/legacyMove) or migrate; (3) a label hands authority to the migration only if some call does. There is no premise on the executor's code.
headlines.witness: ForwardWitness: the succession forward wSuccession is covered from wPost and succeeds. The bundle reaches wPost from wPre.

headlines.meaning: Take any XRun K s xs s' that mixes Authority transactions (.tx l) with forwards, where every forward's calls are covered (sender not the migration or 0; no renounce or code swap). Then ARun K s (xs.flatMap XLabel.labels) s' holds, and a label hands authority to the migration only if some transaction does. So every 'along any run' result of Authority, NoReparkingAfterMigrate included, applies verbatim. Its sender is the owner, the nominee, or (for migrate) the executor. So from such states the labels allow no step that a covered call could not make.
headlines.witness: ForwardWitness: wPost has nonzero owners, and AStep (wConfig true) wPost (.nominate 7) _ exists.

headlines.meaning: Premises: s.executed = true, nothing is parked on the migration at s, and XRun K s xs s'. No transaction hands authority to the migration by an ownership call (nominate M or transferPA M, including inside forwards), and no forward contains a CTM code swap. For each, ¬ ∃ ls, ARun wPost ls s' holds. Underlying invariant (LabelRunsKeepOwnersNonzero): every ARun keeps a nonzero CTM owner and a nonzero ProxyAdmin owner nonzero.

headlines.meaning: Take any FRun K s cs s' in which no call is sent by address 0. (1) If s.paOwner = 0, then s'.paOwner = 0. 1. Solidity, low severity, hardening. Neither the CTM nor the CTM-domain ProxyAdmin disables renounceOwnership, so one forwarded call strands that authority.
   - The CTM is `contract ChainTypeManager is ..., Ownable2StepUpgradeable` (UPG state-transition/ChainTypeManager.sol:58) with no override. OZ's renounceOwnership (lib/openzeppelin-contracts-upgradeable-v4 @2d081f2, contracts/access/OwnableUpgradeable.sol:66-68, via Ownable2StepUpgradeable.sol:51-54) sets owner and pendingOwner to 0.
   - The ProxyAdmin is OZ `ProxyAdmin is Ownable` (lib/openzeppelin-contracts-v4 @dc44c9f, contracts/access/Ownable.sol:61-63), and its renounceOwnership sets the owner to 0.
   - One call inside UpgradeExecutorBase.forward (UPG governance/UpgradeExecutorBase.sol:32-46) has these effects (proved as RenouncedAuthorityIsStranded):
     - the ProxyAdmin becomes permanently ownerless, so the CTM domain's proxies and the CTM's code can never be changed again;
     - the CTM becomes ownerless, recoverable only by a code swap through the ProxyAdmin.
   - This conflicts with the executor's own NatSpec: UpgradeExecutorBase.sol:14-17 says forward exists "so the authority the executor holds never becomes unreachable", and :48-53 disables renounceOwnership on the executor because "an ownerless executor would strand every authority it holds". The authorities it holds keep their own renounce.
   - It needs the executor's owner (governance) to send the call, so it is not an attack. Possible fix: override renounceOwnership to revert in ChainTypeManager, and use a ProxyAdmin that does the same.
   - Note: the OZ submodules are not checked out in the scratchpad e561b9cc2 tree. They were read at the exact submodule commits it pins (2d081f2, dc44c9f) from /Users/samsara/code/custom-stf-e2e/era-contracts-l1-interop/lib.
2. Model, not Solidity. The README's label-set argument (EraSpec/Contracts/RegistryBootstrapMigration/README.md:70-80) is false as stated for renounce.
   - Its "Other actors are over-approximated" list (:64-66) omits renounceOwnership on both the CTM and the ProxyAdmin.
   - A forwarded renounce reaches a state that no run of the existing labels reaches (ForwardedRenounceLeavesTheLabelSet, LabelRunsKeepOwnersNonzero).
   - The parking results survive it (NoReparkingAcrossForwards).
3. Known boundary, made concrete, not new. A forwarded upgradeAndCall on the CTM proxy (OZ ProxyAdmin.sol:74-80; the CTM proxy is administered by CTM_PROXY_ADMIN, CTMUpgradeExecutor.sol:38-40) bypasses every Ownable2Step check. It can write the spent migration into the CTM's owner slot (ForwardCtmSwapReparks). This is the authority-side analogue of ForwardCtmSwapBreaksInvariants.

### Same README: replace the section "## The CTM executor's `forward`" (currently :70-80) with
```
## The CTM executor's `forward` (topic Forward)

`UpgradeExecutorBase.forward` (`governance/UpgradeExecutorBase.sol:32-46`) is modelled as a list of calls, each with its own `msg.sender`:
- the calls `forward` makes, sent by the executor;
- the calls their targets make in turn, sent by those targets.

The entry points are the writers of the tracked slots:
- the CTM's `transferOwnership`, `acceptOwnership`, `renounceOwnership` and owner-only version writers;
- the `ProxyAdmin`'s `transferOwnership` and `renounceOwnership`, and `upgrade`/`upgradeAndCall` on the CTM proxy;
- `migrate()`;
- plus a call that writes nothing tracked.

No premise is made on the executor's code.

- `ForwardIsARun`: a successful forward is a run of this model's labels if none of its calls is sent by the migration or the zero address, renounces an ownership, or replaces the CTM's code. Each call becomes its other-actor label, or `migrate`. The labels hand authority to the migration only where the calls do.
- `RunsWithForwardsAreRuns` lifts this to runs mixing forwards with the model's transactions, so the "along any run" results (`NoReparkingAfterMigrate`, ...) apply to them.
- Conversely, from nonzero owners, each label other than the bundle is one covered call (`LabelsAreCoveredCalls`).
- Stronger direct forms:
  - `NoReparkingAcrossForwards`: no premise on senders, and renounces allowed.
  - `ForwardMovesParkedCTMOnlyByNomineeAccept`: the accept must be the start state's nominee's.
  - `ForwardMovesParkedProxyAdminOnlyByMigrate`: holds even with code swaps.
- **The label set misses `renounceOwnership`.** The CTM (`Ownable2StepUpgradeable`) and the CTM-domain `ProxyAdmin` (OpenZeppelin `Ownable`) both keep it, and a forward can call it.
  - No run of the labels reaches the state it leaves, because those runs keep both owners nonzero (`LabelRunsKeepOwnersNonzero`, `ForwardedRenounceLeavesTheLabelSet`).
  - It parks nothing, but it strands authority (`RenouncedAuthorityIsStranded`, `RenounceStrandsWitness`):
    - an ownerless `ProxyAdmin` never gets an owner again;
    - an ownerless CTM with no nominee gets an owner back only through a code swap by the `ProxyAdmin`'s owner.
- **Excluded: replacing the CTM's code** (`upgrade`/`upgradeAndCall` on the CTM proxy).
  - It can re-park the CTM on the spent migration with no ownership call naming it (`ForwardCtmSwapReparks`).
  - It can move a parked CTM without the nominee's accept (`ForwardCtmSwapMovesParkedCTM`).
  - On the version state it voids the CTM's invariants (`../ChainTypeManager/`, `ForwardCtmSwapBreaksInvariants`).
- Witnesses:
  - `ForwardWitness`: the bundle, then executor succession through `forward`, with the successor's accept as a nested call.
  - `ParkedForwardFramesFire`: a forwarded `acceptOwnership()` recovers the CTM that the non-genuine executor left parked, and a forwarded `migrate()` moves the `ProxyAdmin`.
- Not modelled: `ProxyAdmin.changeProxyAdmin` on the CTM proxy (who administers the CTM proxy is configuration), ETH, events.
```

headlines.meaning: For any TxRun with R 0 = predeploy, one of two cases holds. Either every state is the predeploy and every tx n = none. Or there is a step k such that: the states are the predeploy up to k; no transaction succeeds before k; tx k = some (K.upgrader, initL2); R (k+1) = setup; and fun n => R (k+1+n) is a Run. Companions: PredeployRunStates (each state is the predeploy, or is reached from setup, Valid, and reached from hSetup when paired with the source's own (_leafNumber, _height), so every RunHeight headline applies); PredeployRunReclaimableIffAbsent (at every initialized state and every v ≠ 0, a straddling leaf exists iff v is not a key); TxRunFromValidIsRun (a TxRun from a Valid state is a Run); RunLiftsToTxRun (every Run from setup is the tail of a TxRun from the predeploy whose first transaction is the upgrader's initL2).
headlines.witness: Contracts.InteropCommitmentTree.GenesisRunWitness (predeploy, initL2, insert(a,0), insert(b,1) for 0 < a < b)

headlines.meaning: Track FullMerkle._nodes[0] as a ghost L along the run (LevelRun hl R tx L: each successful transaction applies the source's writes setupLevel or insertLevel; L 0 is arbitrary). Take any node hash h, padding z0, leaf hash hl, TxRun from the predeploy, initialized step n, and any height. If a value v has an accepted inclusion proof and an accepted non-inclusion proof against rootOf h z0 (storedLeaves (L n) (R n).leafCount) height, then one of the two submitted paths carries a located TreeRootBreak. There is no hash premise. It rests on StoredLeavesAreLeafHashes: along every TxRun from the predeploy, storedLeaves (L n) (R n).leafCount = leafHashes hl (R n), so TreeRoot's root is the fold of the contract's own leaf level.
headlines.witness: Contracts.InteropCommitmentTree.StoredRootWitness (premises met at step 3 of genesisRun a b, at the published height 2; the honest inclusion path has no break and the padding-forged absence path has the paddingHit break)

headlines.meaning: Countermodel with IMTAlreadyInitialized deleted (TxStepNoGuard; nothing else changed). For any roles and a ≠ 0, reinitRun is the guardless run: predeploy, then initL2 gives setup, then insert(a,0), then a second initL2 by the upgrader. So it has two successful initL2 calls (steps 0 and 2), and the deployed TxStep has no step for the second. The final state is initialized with leaves {0,0,0}, {a,0,0}, {0,0,0} and valueToIndex a = 1. a is still a key and is straddled by a zero leaf, so 'reclaimable iff absent' fails at step 3. The state is not Valid, and the history projected from setup on is neither an Evolution nor a GuardedEvolution. Its first state has value 0 at index 0.
headlines.witness: countermodel (self-witnessing)

headlines.meaning: Countermodel at the hash level, on the same guardless run with its ghost _nodes[0] (reinitLevel). After the second initL2: storedLeaves = [hl {0,1,a}, hl {a,0,0}, hl {0,0,0}], because index 0 keeps the sentinel's pre-reset hash. The list state's leafHashes are [hl {0,0,0}, hl {a,0,0}, hl {0,0,0}], and fmHeight 3 = 2. Against rootOf h z0 storedLeaves 2, both an honest inclusion proof of a (index 1) and an honest non-inclusion proof of a with leaf {0,0,0} (index 2) are accepted, for every h, z0 and hl. No collision and no forged sibling is needed.
headlines.witness: countermodel (self-witnessing)

headlines.meaning: This refutes the backlog sentence 'drop the guard and the reset countermodel fires'. On the guardless machine, every run whose first state has value 0 at index 0 (the predeploy, setup, and every Valid tree do) has a key set that never shrinks. The same holds for GuardlessResetHistoryUnreachable: for a ≠ 0, no stretch of such a run projects to resetHistory a. The source's setup never erases a key; the guard protects the sentinel link (GapSound), not the key set. The weakest true repaired form is GuardlessReinitBreaksExclusivity.

prove.sourceFindings:
No Solidity defect found. The NatSpec claims checked all hold in the model. These are: one-time seeding, and '_imt.setup() reverts if the tree was already seeded' (L2InteropCommitmentTree.sol:43-46, IL2InteropCommitmentTree.sol:19-20, 48); '_leafNumber != 0 serves as the initialized flag' (L2InteropCommitmentTree.sol:30-32); and 'append-only' (L2InteropCommitmentTree.sol:30), which is true of values at occupied indices, while insert rewrites the low leaf's links by design.

Two hypothetical-only observations, unreachable at the pin because the guard exists:
- A re-run of IMT.setup would write leaves[0] = {0,0,0} (IndexedMerkleTree.sol:50) without updateLeaf. That would leave _nodes[0][0] stale, so the list state and the hash tree would disagree.
- A re-run of FullMerkle.setup would push stray entries onto _zeros and _nodes (FullMerkle.sol:31-32). These are read once _height reaches 3; this was checked by hand, not proved.

Repo-spec narrative issue (not Solidity): the ResetAndZero header (IndexedMerkleTree/Specs/ResetAndZero.lean and its Properties/Proofs copies) says a re-initialization would 'ERASE every delivered leg from the key set'. At the source, a re-run of setup erases no key (GuardlessRunsKeepKeys). The double spend it would enable comes instead from the reset sentinel link and the appended zero leaf (GuardlessReinitBreaksExclusivity, GuardlessReinitForgesAbsenceAtStoredRoot).

review.sourceFindingAssessment:
The prover reports no Solidity defect, which I confirm. The guard is real: IndexedMerkleTree.sol:43-45 reverts with IMTAlreadyInitialized when _leafNumber != 0. onlyUpgrader is at L2InteropCommitmentTree.sol:36-41, and the appender check at :54. initL2 is called once, only in the ZKsync OS genesis upgrade (L2GenesisForceDeploymentsHelper.sol:458-461). The proxy's only initial storage is the EIP-1967 slots (genesis.rs:330-338), so _imt starts as all-zero storage.

Both hypothetical observations are correct. (a) A re-run of setup writes leaves[0] = {0,0,0} (IndexedMerkleTree.sol:50) without updateLeaf. FullMerkle.setup (FullMerkle.sol:31-32) does not touch _nodes[0], and pushNewLeaf writes only index _leafNumber, so _nodes[0][0] keeps the hash of {0,1,a}. (b) The stray _zeros.push/_nodes.push (FullMerkle.sol:31-32) lands at index height+1. In the reinit trace, _nodes[2][0] is rewritten by updateLeaf (FullMerkle.sol:91) using only _zeros[0..1], so the stray _zeros[2] is read only once _height reaches 3, as claimed.

The repo-narrative finding is also real. ResetAndZero.lean:18 says re-initialization would 'ERASE' delivered keys. setupWrites, which matches the source, keeps every leaf value at indices >= 1 and all of valueToIndex, and GuardlessRunsKeepKeys proves keys are kept. The real guardless hazard is the reset sentinel link plus the stale _nodes[0][0], proved in GuardlessReinitBreaksExclusivity and GuardlessReinitForgesAbsenceAtStoredRoot. None of these is a Solidity bug at the pin.

Nothing in O3 (a), (b) or (c) is left unproved. Everything below is model boundary or correspondence work.

**Boundaries the model rests on (now `MODEL-HANDLER-REENTRY`):**
- Re-entry happens only at the target's `receiveMessage` (`InteropHandlerBase.sol:282-286`). This needs three facts:
  - `_proveInclusion` and `requireFlowFinalized` are static calls (`view`; `common/interfaces/IMessageVerification.sol:18-24`, `atomic-interop/IAtomicFlowManager.sol:53`);
  - `_handleCallValue`'s path through `BaseTokenHolder.give` reaches no entry point (`l2-system/BaseTokenHolder.sol:99-109`, `bridge/asset-tracker/L2AssetTracker.sol:359-380`);
  - the target's effect on handler state goes only through entry-point calls.
  These are argued in the Specs docstring, not proved (`VM-CALL`, `DEP-FRAME`).
- Nested rollback is the model's `Option` rule (`VM-REVERT`, `SOL-CONTROL`).
- Reject-only checks are omitted: permissions, destination context, versions, pause, and selector/value checks. Omitting them only adds runs.
  - So the countermodels assume a bundle that lets the re-entering target in: no execution address, and the target named as unbundler.
  - `executeAtomicBundle` is included for the L1 handler as well, which also only adds runs.

**Not stated:**
- Generic enabledness of the unbundled route (only witnesses show it).
- Liveness of a retry when targets keep reverting (`OPS-PROGRESS`).

prove.item: R3. Router: run-level NoHijack under a logged, bounded premise

headlines.meaning: This is the headline. Take any encoding enc, chain thisChain, vault address ntv, normalised vault address ntvAddr, ANY start router R0, end router R and call log, where R is reached from R0 by exactly the logged guarded calls of _setAssetHandlerAddressThisChain (ReachLog). Take any (chain, sender, data) triple q such that enc is injective on loggedTriples(log) together with q. Then the handler at enc q in R is the handler argument of the last logged call whose triple is q, or R0's handler there if no call hashed q. The tracker at enc q is that call's msg.sender, or R0's tracker. So no call hashing a different triple moved the route, whether it differs in sender, data or chain. The guard is not used (RouteIsLastOwnWriteWithoutGuard states the same for unguarded applyCalls).
headlines.witness: Contracts.AssetRouter.LoggedRouteIsLastOwnWriteSatisfiable

headlines.meaning: Take any logged run ReachLog R0 R log from any R0, and any step in it: log = pre ++ c :: post, S is reached from R0 by pre, and StepCall c S T. Suppose c.caller != ntv. Then for every sender s != c.caller and data d' such that enc is injective on loggedTriples(log) plus (thisChain, s, d'), T.handler(enc thisChain s d') = S.handler(enc thisChain s d').
headlines.witness: Contracts.AssetRouter.LoggedRunNoHijackSatisfiable

headlines.meaning: This is the same as LoggedRunNoHijack for a step whose caller IS the vault (c.caller = ntv). The vault skips the tracker check, and anyone can trigger its call through registerToken. For every s != ntvAddr and every d' such that enc is injective on loggedTriples(log) plus (thisChain, s, d'), the step leaves the handler at enc thisChain s d' unchanged.
headlines.witness: Contracts.AssetRouter.LoggedRunNtvTouchesOnlyItsOwnIdsSatisfiable

headlines.meaning: This combines the guard with the bounded premise. Take any logged run R0 -> R from any R0, any sender s != ntvAddr, and any d' such that enc is injective on loggedTriples(log) plus (thisChain, s, d'). Then R.tracker(enc thisChain s d') = R0.tracker(enc thisChain s d'). If the handler there changed, then R0's tracker there is s and the log contains a call by s with data d'.
headlines.witness: Contracts.AssetRouter.LoggedRunCustomRouteAnswersToRegistrantSatisfiable

headlines.meaning: This is R3's statement with exactly its planned premise. Take any logged run R0 -> R from any R0 such that enc is injective on loggedTriples(log), with no extra triple. Suppose log = pre ++ c :: post, c.caller = ntv, and no vault call in post has data c.data. Then R.handler(enc thisChain ntvAddr c.data) = c.handler and R.tracker(enc thisChain ntvAddr c.data) = ntv. In words, a route the vault installed survives every later call, whether non-vault or a vault call for other data.
headlines.witness: Contracts.AssetRouter.LoggedRunKeepsVaultRoutesSatisfiable (premise necessity in the model: countermodel CollidingVaultCallMovesVaultRoute)

headlines.meaning: This takes NO hash premise. From any router S, suppose the vault's call c (c.caller = ntv) steps S to S', and then a logged run of calls, none by ntv, goes from S' to T. Then T.handler(enc thisChain ntvAddr c.data) = c.handler and T.tracker(enc thisChain ntvAddr c.data) = ntv. It follows from VaultTrackerIsPermanent and NonVaultRunKeepsVaultRoutes, both hash-free.
headlines.witness: Contracts.AssetRouter.VaultRouteGuardSatisfiable

headlines.meaning: This takes no hash premise and does not need the guard. Take any logged run R0 -> R in which every vault call names ntv itself as handler, as the only vault call site does (NativeTokenVaultBase.sol:518-521). If every id with tracker ntv in R0 has handler ntv, then every id with tracker ntv in R has handler ntv.
headlines.witness: Contracts.AssetRouter.VaultHeldRoutesPointAtVaultSatisfiable

headlines.meaning: This takes no premise beyond the run. In every logged run of the single-writer model from fresh storage (empty), every call's caller is ntv. OnlyVaultActsAmidOtherWriters says the same when arbitrary tracker-preserving writes are interleaved, which covers the other L2 writers.
headlines.witness: Contracts.AssetRouter.FromEmptyWitness

headlines.meaning: Take any logged run R0 -> R and any triple q that no logged call hashed, with enc injective on loggedTriples(log) plus q. Then the handler and tracker at enc q are unchanged from R0. This covers ids hashed with another chain's id, which is how the L1 counterpart's ids appear on L2.
headlines.witness: Contracts.AssetRouter.LoggedRunLeavesUnhashedRoutesSatisfiable

headlines.meaning: Countermodel: the bounded premise cannot be dropped. Start from the storage the owner's setAssetDeploymentTracker(d', s) leaves on fresh storage. Registrant s sets a live route h. Then one vault call for token data d, whose id collides with s's id, repoints s's live route to the vault and records the vault as tracker, and s fails the guard for its own asset. The two colliding triples are both logged, so IdInjOn on loggedTriples fails.
headlines.witness: countermodel (self-witnessing existential)

headlines.meaning: Countermodel: with the require deleted (applyCalls), a non-vault caller whose address is ntvAddr (possible only if ntv != ntvAddr, i.e. on L1) overwrites the vault's route, even though enc is injective on the run's triples. With the guard that call is rejected. So the vault-route protection is the guard's, not the hash's.
headlines.witness: countermodel (self-witnessing existential)

headlines.meaning: Countermodel: without its premise, LoggedRunKeepsVaultRoutes fails in the model. From empty, the vault registers d naming itself, then registers d' != d with a colliding id naming handler h != ntv. The route for d now points at h. The deployed vault never names another handler.
headlines.witness: countermodel (self-witnessing existential)

prove.sourceFindings:
No contradiction between the pinned Solidity and its NatSpec was found for this item. Three observations follow.

(1) On L2, `setAssetHandlerAddressThisChain` can only ever succeed for the L2 native token vault (NTV), assuming the router's storage starts fresh.
- The tracker mapping has exactly two writers. One is `AssetRouterBase.sol:83`, which records `msg.sender` after the guard at `:81`. The other is `L1AssetRouter.sol:159-166`, which is L1-only and `onlyOwner`.
- The other L2 writers (`L2AssetRouter.sol:167` `initL2`, `:200-206` `setAssetHandlerAddress`, and the `AssetRouterBase.sol:285-286` `_finalizeDeposit` fallback) all go through `_setAssetHandler` at `:298-301`, which writes the handler only.
- So every L2 tracker is 0 or the NTV. This is proved as `OnlyVaultActsFromEmpty` and `OnlyVaultActsAmidOtherWriters`.
- This is consistent with `AssetRouterBase.sol:61` ("on the chain of the asset deployment tracker"). But the sentence at `:63-64` ("custom tokens may have their own specific asset deployment trackers") holds on L1 only, and only after the owner's `setAssetDeploymentTracker`. The custom tracker in use at the pin is `CTMDeploymentTracker.sol:71-91`.

(2) Minor, owner-only: `L1AssetRouter.setAssetDeploymentTracker` (`L1AssetRouter.sol:159-166`) does not check `_assetDeploymentTracker != address(0)`.
- With 0 it can only zero the tracker of an id hashed from sender 0, and no guarded call hashes sender 0.
- This is relevant to R2's `RunValid` analysis, not to R3.

(3) The repo docs, not the Solidity: `EraSpec/Contracts/AssetRouterBase/Properties/HandlerRegistration.lean:19-22` says a custom tracker "has to be bootstrapped through the native token vault or the L1-to-L2 counterpart path".
- Neither path records a custom tracker. The vault's call records the vault (`OnlyVaultActsFromEmpty`), and the counterpart's `setAssetHandlerAddress` writes only the handler.
- The only bootstrap is L1's owner-only `setAssetDeploymentTracker`.
- I did not edit that docstring; a replacement is in `docUpdates`.

R3 is fully proved as stated, and extended. Its planned statement holds with exactly the planned premise (`LoggedRunKeepsVaultRoutes`). Against non-vault callers it also holds with no hash premise at all (`NtvRouteSurvivesNonVaultCalls`).

What stays open:
1. **Other writers are not steps of the runs.** The runs model only the single writer `_setAssetHandlerAddressThisChain`. L1's owner-only `setAssetDeploymentTracker`, the L2 counterpart's `setAssetHandlerAddress`, `_finalizeDeposit`'s handler fallback and the initializers are covered only as whatever they left in an arbitrary start router R0.
   - On L1, owner tracker writes in the middle of a run are outside the results.
   - On L2 the other writers are covered abstractly, as arbitrary tracker-preserving writes, but only for the guard result `OnlyVaultActsAmidOtherWriters`, not for the route results.
   - Adding them as real steps is R2.
2. **Fresh storage is assumed.** The L2 reading of `OnlyVaultActsAmidOtherWriters` assumes the router's storage starts fresh. An upgrade that wrote the tracker mapping would be outside it (OPS-CONFIG).
3. **No reduction-style form.** The run-level premise is `IdInjOn` on `loggedTriples(log)` plus the watched triple. No collision-finding statement is given.
4. **Not modelled:** events, ABI encoding of the id preimage (`enc` is abstract), and router storage/call correspondence.
5. **Vault re-registration of the same data.** `LoggedRunKeepsVaultRoutes` excludes a later vault call with the same data. In the deployed vault that call cannot happen, because `registerToken` requires the token to be unregistered, but that vault-side fact is not linked here.

All three observations are real. None of them is a contradiction in the Solidity.

(1) Real. The tracker mapping is written only at AssetRouterBase.sol:83 and L1AssetRouter.sol:164. The second is the L1-only, onlyOwner setAssetDeploymentTracker at :159-166. Every other handler writer goes through _setAssetHandler (:298-301), which writes the handler only: L2AssetRouter.sol:167 initL2, :205 setAssetHandlerAddress (onlyAssetRouterCounterpart), AssetRouterBase.sol:286 _finalizeDeposit, and L1AssetRouter.sol:144 setNativeTokenVault. On L2, _nativeTokenVaultAddr() is L2_NATIVE_TOKEN_VAULT_ADDR (L2AssetRouter.sol:72-73), and nothing on L2 calls setAssetHandlerAddressThisChain except the vault at NativeTokenVaultBase.sol:518. So from fresh storage only the NTV ever passes the require at :81. This is consistent with the NatSpec at :61-64, read as L1-only for custom trackers.

(2) Real and minor. L1AssetRouter.sol:159-166 has no zero-address check on _assetDeploymentTracker. It is owner-only and harmless here.

(3) Real, in the repo's own docs. Properties/HandlerRegistration.lean:19-22 says a custom tracker 'has to be bootstrapped through the native token vault or the L1-to-L2 counterpart path'. That is wrong: the vault's call records msg.sender, which is the vault (:83), and L2AssetRouter.setAssetHandlerAddress (:200-206) writes the handler only. The only bootstrap is L1's owner-only setAssetDeploymentTracker. The proposed docstring replacement is correct.
